nodes.name: Ni foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Cut the nickel foam into a rectangle (2 cm × 4 cm), and then use acetone, 3 M hydrochloric acid, ethanol, and deionized water to ultrasonically treat for 10 min to remove the surface oil and oxide layer.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal sulfurization
nodes.procedure: Nickel sulfate hexahydrate and sodium thiosulfate pentahydrate were dissolved in 60 ml deionized water at 1:3 molar ratio, and then 0.1g PVP was added and stirred at room temperature for 20 min to obtain a transparent solution. The solution was transferred to a 100 ml stainless steel autoclave with a piece of pretreated nickel foam (2 cm × 4 cm), reacted at 170°C for 10 h; after the reaction, the nickel foam was thoroughly washed with deionized water and ethanol and dried at 80°C for 6 h to obtain Ni3S2/NF.

nodes.name: Electrochemical reconstruction
nodes.procedure: Ni3S2/NF-R was obtained by placing Ni3S2/NF in 1 M KOH solution and performing CV cycling at 5 mV/s until the redox current density remains basically unchanged in the voltage range of 0.83-1.68V (vs. RHE). The figure of the initial 20 CV cycles reconstruction process is shown in Fig. S1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Clear diffraction peaks at 21.8°, 31.1°, 23.8°, 49.7°, and 55.4° demonstrate successful fabrication of hexagonal Ni3S2 (JCPDS No. 44-1418). After CV activation, Ni3S2 peaks almost disappear indicating amorphization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: clear diffraction peaks centered at 21.8°, 31.1°, 23.8°, 49.7°, and 55.4° are well resolved in the X-ray powder diffraction pattern (Fig. 1b), demonstrating the successful fabrication of hexagonal Ni3S2 ... After 1000 CV cycles, diffraction peaks of Ni3S2 almost disappears in the reconstructed Ni3S2/NF (denoted as Ni3S2/NF-R)

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine Ni3S2/NF shows interspersed thin nanoflakes vertically planted on nickel foam substrate. After activation, free-standing nanoflakes transform into honeycomb-like structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1c, interspersed thin nanoflakes are planted vertically on the nickel foamed substrate ... Significant morphology evolution takes place with free-standing nanoflakes transformed into a honeycomb-like structure (Fig. 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals slightly curly nanoflakes. HRTEM shows lattice fringes with 2.43 Å spacing for (003) plane of Ni3S2. After activation, 2.08 Å d-spacing corresponds to (105) plane of NiOOH with amorphous layer on pore walls.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image reveals the slightly curly appearance of the nanoflakes (Fig. 1d). In addition, the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Fig. 1e) displays clear lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of 2.43 Å, pointing to the (003) plane of Ni3S2 ... the (105) crystal facet of a d-spacing of 2.08 Å is in agreement with the crystal phase of NiOOH ... continuous amorphous layer domains the pore wall

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Ni and S elements in Ni3S2/NF. After activation, sharp decrease of S content with rapid increase of O content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: energy dispersive spectrum (EDS) element mapping (Fig. S1a, Supporting Information) of Ni3S2/NF provides intuitive evidence for the uniform distribution of Ni and S elements ... a sharp decrease of S content takes place combined with a rapid increase of O content in Ni3S2/NF-R according to the EDS element mapping result (Fig. S2 and Table S1)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p: 855.34 eV (2p3/2, Ni2+), 872.91 eV (2p1/2); S 2p: 162.03 eV (S-Ni), 168.21 eV (SO4^2-). After 20 CV cycles: NiOOH at 856.11 eV (Ni3+), Ni-S weakens, SO4^2- retains.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum can be fitted into Ni 2p3/2 at 855.34 eV and Ni 2p1/2 at 872.91 eV, indicating the presence of Ni2+. ... In the S 2p spectrum (Fig. 1j), two peaks located at 162.03 and 168.21 eV ... After 20 cycles of CV activation, the peak of nickel sulfide is significantly weakened and NiOOH characteristic peak appears at 856.11eV

nodes.characterization_summary: At OCP: Ni-S at 200, 222, 301, 322, 348 cm^-1. At 1.33 V vs RHE: Ni-O bending at 485.3 cm^-1, stretching at 562.9 cm^-1 indicating NiOOH formation. Negative peak shift before 1.53 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: characteristic peaks of Ni-S bonds at 200, 222, 301, 322, and 348 cm^-1 are detected ... After the applied potential increases to 1.33 V (vs. RHE), two weak peaks centered at 485.3 cm^-1 and 562.9 cm^-1, corresponding to the bending vibration Ni-O bond and stretching vibration of Ni-O bond

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl = 45.91 mF cm^-2 for Ni3S2/NF-R (vs 23.61 mF cm^-2 pristine, 1.53 mF cm^-2 NiOOH/NF) indicating higher ECSA after reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The obtained Cdl of Ni3S2/NF-R (45.91 mF cm^-2) is much larger than that of pristine Ni3S2/NF (23.61 mF cm^2) and NiOOH/NF (1.53 mF cm^-2)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni3S2/NF-R shows lower resistance indicating better OER charge transfer kinetics. Bode plots show electron conduction faster than interface charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) results show that Ni3S2/NF-R has lower resistance than the other two samples ... the phase angle of the high-frequency region in the Bode diagram is much smaller than that of the low-frequency region

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl = 45.91 mF cm^-2 for Ni3S2/NF-R vs 23.61 mF cm^-2 for pristine Ni3S2/NF, indicating higher ECSA after electrochemical activation-induced reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The obtained Cdl of Ni3S2/NF-R (45.91 mF cm^-2) is much larger than that of pristine Ni3S2/NF (23.61 mF cm^2) and NiOOH/NF (1.53 mF cm^-2), indicating that electrochemical activation-induced structure reconstruction is conducive to promoting the exposure of active sites
